📚 Toward a Revolution in the Statism Paradigm (Rethinking Governance in Light of Global Transformations) | Volume One: Theoretical Pathology of Governance | Authors: Reza Shahran, Hossein Vazifeh-Ali | First Edition | Naqd-e Farhang Publishing | 1405 | The modern state has been one of the most successful institutions in human history. Security, public education, economic development, the formation of modern nations, and many achievements of the contemporary world would have been inconceivable without it. But can a structure formed to solve the problems of centuries past still respond to today's networked world, artificial intelligence, the digital economy, and interconnected societies? This book begins with a fundamental question: Why do many governance systems, despite repeated reforms, changes of government, restructuring, and accumulated experience, still find themselves reproducing similar crises, imbalances, and dissatisfactions? Drawing on political philosophy, governance theory, complexity science, futures studies, and historical experience, the author shows that many contemporary problems cannot be understood merely at the level of performance, institutions, or policies; instead, we must return to the deeper layer of governance theories and the foundational assumptions upon which these structures were built. Toward a Revolution in the Statism Paradigm is, before it is a book about solutions, a book about diagnosing the problem — an effort to examine the pathology of dominant governance theories and to identify the source of the blockages that manifest as inefficiency, concentration of power, legitimacy crises, and the inability to solve complex problems. This work is the first volume of a broader research project. In subsequent volumes, building on the pathologies presented in this book, an alternative theory of governance will be developed — one that seeks to articulate, within a coherent framework, the capacities of the networked world, human agency, and the distribution of knowledge and power. A transition model suited to Iran's conditions will also be presented, spanning from the level of theoretical foundations to that of macro-policymaking and institutional design, in order to explore the possibility of a gradual movement from the existing situation toward emerging orders. This book seeks not the elimination of order, but an order capable of organizing the freedom, agency, and complexity of the contemporary world without an ever-increasing concentration of power.🛒To purchase the book, click on this link🛒🟠Join Naqd-e Farhang on Instagram🟠@naqdefarhangpub.

📚 Between Bone and Soul (a collection of blank verse poetry) | Poet: Yousef Sheikhi | First edition | Naqd-e Farhang Publishing | 1405 | This book is the journey of thought in pursuit of the invisible breath of meaning; somewhere between bone and soul, where the word reflects upon itself so that it might perhaps pass beyond the skin of death and faith. In this book, more than anything, I have thought about the dot — the very dot in which all secrets lie hidden. In a dotless preface — "The Treatise of Consolation" — language, with no dot to lean on, becomes a form of prayer; a prayer for the human who still believes in their own presence. In the long blank verses, philosophy takes refuge in poetry. René Descartes in the solitude of his doubt, Nietzsche in the brightness of his madness, Plato on the precipice of shadows, and Buber in the endless dialogue between I and Thou — all join the poet in seeking the sacred. In the short blank verses, the world becomes a particle: Gaza is drenched in blood, a child cries, the violinist of Tehran's bright nights plays for a nameless angel; and behind every event, an invisible hand seeks meaning. This book is a ritual for recognizing the human anew, and a remembrance for the God who stands in prayer within the human body.🛒To purchase the book, click on this link🛒🟠Join Naqd-e Farhang on Instagram🟠@naqdefarhangpub.

In this promised vision, structural war grounded in conflict will fade away, and human societies will live alongside one another in complete ontological harmony. The reason for the realization of this permanent peace will be the absolute absence of any "oppression" in a global sphere that recognizes the territorial integrity of the human being; in other words, the ultimate cause of wars is rooted in the institutionalization of oppression in the interactions of human societies, and with the elimination of discrimination and aggression, the material and spiritual ground for war will also vanish. Therefore, understanding the roots of oppression is a necessary preliminary to understanding why bloody conflicts persist in the contemporary world. This understanding establishes a deep link between sustainable peace and the eradication of injustice, which can be regarded as the main foundation of contemporary philosophical dialogues. Such a view of history distances us from political simplifications and guides us toward understanding the existential roots of crises. However, the main question here is: how can we move from the current situation toward that promised future? This transition requires a collective will grounded in transcendental awareness that is defined beyond narrow national interests; therefore, understanding war is itself the beginning of a path that leads to sustainable and ethical peace.🛒To purchase the book, click on this link🛒🟠Join Naqd-e Farhang on Instagram🟠@naqdefarhangpub.

◼️Condolence message from Dr. #Reza_Soleyman_Heshmat on the passing of Dr. Mohammad Reza Rikhtehgaran
The late Dr. Mohammad Reza Rikhtehgaran was a highly virtuous person with a remarkable inner calm and tranquility. He learned a great deal from the late Professor Seyyed Ahmad Fardid and Professor Davari Ardakani, especially in the fields of art and poetry. He also spent time in India researching ancient texts and the culture of the subcontinent, and upon his return, he took on the teaching of the course on wisdom in Asia and the East at the University of Tehran. He was deeply committed to contemplative thought and the philosophical and wisdom traditions in the history of Eastern and Western philosophy. If he leaned toward one side in matters of belief and politics, he never abandoned fairness and moderation.
One of my unforgettable memories with him—after which I never had the chance to see him again—was when, at the invitation of Dr. Ayatollahi, it was arranged for me to speak on "Paradoxy" in Hafez, Kierkegaard, and Nietzsche at the House of Humanities Thinkers, and he was to serve as the discussant. It was a good session. Afterward, he called and expressed his kindness and appreciation. What I remember is that I said the core point, of course in Derrida's terms, goes back to Heidegger's two-fold dialectic and the late Fardid's insights on opposites, but the detailed exposition was my own, and naturally any errors or shortcomings in it were mine.
Once again, I ask God Almighty for forgiveness, mercy, and elevation of rank for the deceased, and for patience and reward for his family, friends, and admirers. Undoubtedly, Iran's academic and scholarly community will always benefit from his written works, God willing.
🖋 Reza Soleyman Heshmat
1405/06/11
